description: A heavy non-drying vegetable oil used as the liquid base of a leather dressing. It carries the dissolved wax into the leather and supplies the lasting oily film that keeps an old binding supple without going hard.
name: castor oil

source_ref.label: Douglas Cockerell, Bookbinding and the Care of Books (1902), Chapter XXII, p.302. Internet Archive.
